title: UE5 plugin ignores set.property, so panel writes, PIE and teleport do nothing
body:
## Summary
The UE5 bridge plugin logs each set.property frame and discards it, so every write the Bidirectional State Sync panel sends has no effect in the editor.

## Description
The plugin's PofWebSocketServer.cpp handles set.property by logging at Verbose, with the comment that full implementation requires FRemoteControlModule. The panel routes three features through that frame: property write-back (src/components/modules/project-setup/BidirectionalStateSyncPanel/useBidirectionalStateSyncPanel.ts:78-88), PIE control via PIECommand and viewport teleport via /Editor/ViewportClient. Neither of those two targets is a real UObject property, so implementing reflection writes would not enable them; they need their own commands. The ledger can never reach confirmed through a write, and a watched row stays at sent or applying. The same plugin hardcodes pieState.elapsedSeconds to 0.0, so the panel shows Running 0.0s for a whole session. Fixed means the plugin applies property writes and handles PIE and camera commands, or the panel stops offering controls the plugin cannot perform.

## Flow
- Open Project Setup, connect the live channel, press Play or Teleport Camera
- Hook sends set.property; the socket accepts it and the log records a normal send
- Plugin logs at Verbose and returns; the editor does not change
- Decide: implement in the UE plugin, or hide the three controls until it exists

## Expected impact
Operators stop being shown working controls that do nothing. A plugin change needs an editor rebuild; hiding controls removes a visible feature until then.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - panel controls reflect what the editor can do
Before: 1 set.property handler, 0 write calls in it; 0 occurrences of PIECommand in the plugin source grep
After: not taken; requires a UE plugin change and a running editor
Method: probe - read the handler and grepped the plugin source; a live editor was out of bounds for this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: C:/Users/kazda/Documents/Unreal Projects/PoF/Plugins/PillarsOfFortuneBridge/Source/PillarsOfFortuneBridgeEditor/Private/PofWebSocketServer.cpp:184-195 logs 'Property write request' then: 'For now, log the request - full implementation requires FRemoteControlModule'. Same file :279 SetNumberField elapsedSeconds 0.0. Grep PIECommand across the plugin .cpp files: no match.

title: Live frames are trusted unvalidated and watch times use a non-wall clock
body:
## Summary
The WS client casts inbound frames without checking them, and watch rows format a plugin timestamp that is not wall-clock time.

## Description
src/lib/ue5-bridge/ws-live-state.ts:240 casts JSON.parse to WSInboundMessage and handleSnapshot stores the payload directly. LiveStateSyncPanel renders snapshot.viewport.viewMode, fov.toFixed and selectedActors.length with no guard (src/components/modules/project-setup/LiveStateSyncPanel/ViewportSection.tsx:28 and :44, SelectionSection.tsx:41), while the bidirectional hook guards snapshot?.viewport (useBidirectionalStateSyncPanel.ts:118), so one malformed frame throws in render on one panel only. Separately the plugin stamps frames with FPlatformTime::Seconds()*1000, time since an arbitrary origin, and WatchesSection renders it through new Date as an 'updated HH:MM:SS' freshness claim (LiveStateSyncPanel/helpers.ts:20, WatchesSection.tsx:61). Fixed means one validation door at frame intake and an arrival time stamped by the client. Both belong in ws-live-state.ts, owned by the ue5-bridge-client context this wave.

## Flow
- Validate state.snapshot shape at intake and log a warning on rejection
- Stamp property.update with client arrival time
- Assert a viewport-less snapshot does not throw and the row shows the arrival clock

## Expected impact
A plugin version mismatch degrades to a logged rejection instead of crashing the panel, and the freshness label becomes true. Could reject frames from an older plugin that omit a field the validator requires.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - malformed frames cannot crash the panel, freshness is real
Before: 0 shape checks at intake; 3 unguarded render reads; timestamp source is FPlatformTime
After: predicted 0 throws on a viewport-less frame; arrival-based clock
Method: simulation - walked the frame path; the file is another context's this wave
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/ue5-bridge/ws-live-state.ts:240 'JSON.parse(event.data as string) as WSInboundMessage'; :327 handleSnapshot stores payload. src/components/modules/project-setup/LiveStateSyncPanel/ViewportSection.tsx:28,44. Plugin PofWebSocketServer.cpp:207,309,466 'FPlatformTime::Seconds() * 1000.0'.
instrument: Vitest with a fake socket: push a state.snapshot without viewport into LiveStateSyncPanel and assert no throw; push property.update with a platform-clock timestamp and assert the rendered clock matches the mocked Date.now arrival time
